intro.title: Build typed parser combinator basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a basic typed parser combinator library in TypeScript. You will learn how to create small, reusable parsing functions that can be combined to handle more complex input structures. The core concept involves using TypeScript's type system to ensure your parsers are type-safe and predictable. You'll work with fundamental TypeScript constructs like functions, generics, and custom types. By the end, you'll have a simple yet powerful toolkit for parsing structured text with full type support.
intro.usecase: Parser combinators are foundational in real-world applications that process structured text, such as form validation libraries, configuration file readers, and domain-specific language interpreters. For example, when building a dashboard that imports CSV data, typed parser combinators ensure each column is correctly parsed into its expected type (numbers, dates, strings) before visualization. In UI development, they power safe, incremental parsing of user input in complex form builders or query editors, providing immediate type feedback. This pattern is also key in tools like code editors' syntax highlighters or API request/response validators, where structured text must be reliably decomposed and validated.
